outcome: Not settled as of 13 October 2026: since 26 January 2024 no event has moved the infimum αₖ for any k in a verified way; the in-window changes are log-power improvements to Ω-lower bounds (Sourmelidis 2024, Mahatab 2025, Lamzouri 2026 for k=2, and number-field analogues in 2025 and 2026), explicit constants or bounds valid only above very large thresholds (Tudzi 2025, Palojärvi and Tudzi 2026), and a claimed but unreadable improvement of αₖ for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20 (Runbo Li, 2025 preprint), while the best upper bounds I could find for αₖ (α₂ ≤ 0.3144831759741 from Li and Yang, 2023; α₉–α₂₁ from Trudgian and Yang, 2023) predate the window.
problem_asks: Statement as frozen (Wikipedia, January 2024): 'Piltz divisor problem on bounding Δₖ(x) = Dₖ(x) − x Pₖ(log x)'. Unpacked from the statement alone: (1) Objects: for each k (the wording names no value of k, so it quantifies over all k; the Piltz section of the same article treats k ≥ 2), Dₖ(x) = Σ_{n≤x} dₖ(n), where dₖ(n) counts ordered factorisations of n into k positive integers; Pₖ is a polynomial of degree k−1 giving the main term; Δₖ(x) is the error term. (2) Upper bounds: for each k, bounds Δₖ(x) = O(x^(θ+ε)) for every ε > 0, i.e. the infimum αₖ of admissible θ. Each k is a separate instance; a bound for one k does not settle the others. (3) Lower bounds: the word 'bounding' could also cover Ω-type lower bounds (how large Δₖ(x) is infinitely often). The bullet does not say whether it does, so both sides are listed. (4) Exact value of αₖ: the conjectured value (k−1)/(2k) (Titchmarsh; for k=2 the Hardy–Landau value 1/4 as the lower side). The bullet does not assert this conjecture; it is listed as context for what 'settled' would mean. Scope note: in the standard convention the Dirichlet divisor problem is the k=2 case; the frozen page's own sub-bullet calls it k=1, which conflicts with its Piltz section (see summary).

events.what_happened: G. H. Hardy (1916) showed that the classical divisor remainder is not o(x^(1/4)), so α₂ ≥ 1/4. Secondary summaries attribute to Hardy the general lower bound αₖ ≥ (k−1)/(2k). The 1916 paper itself was not opened; the k=2 statement is taken from the abstract of Bordellès and Daval (arXiv 2601.01905), which I opened.
events.delivers: Lower bound for k=2: Δ(x) is not O(x^θ) for θ < 1/4, so α₂ ≥ 1/4. For general k, per secondary summaries only, αₖ ≥ (k−1)/(2k). This is the lower side of the conjectured value.
events.remains: The upper side for every k, and the exact value of αₖ for every k.
events.direction: Lower side only. Consistent with the conjectured exponent (k−1)/(2k) and does not touch upper bounds.

events.what_happened: K. Soundararajan, 'Omega results for the divisor and circle problems' (arXiv:math/0302010, 1 Feb 2003; Int. Math. Res. Not. 2003, no. 36, per the reference list in Lamzouri arXiv:2605.21476). The abstract, which I opened, says it gives new Ω-results for the error terms of two classical lattice point problems, 'likely to be the best possible'. Its general-k Piltz Ω form (x-exponent (k−1)/(2k)) is attributed to Soundararajan's method in secondary summaries; I did not verify that in the primary text.
events.revisions: Journal version Int. Math. Res. Not. 2003 no. 36 (per reference list in arXiv:2605.21476; not separately opened).
events.delivers: Ω-lower bounds for the k=2 divisor error term and the circle error term at the conjectured x-exponent, up to log factors (per abstract). For k ≥ 3, per secondary summaries only, the same x-exponent (k−1)/(2k) with log-power factors; not verified.
events.remains: Upper bounds for every αₖ; the sign of the large values; the sharp log powers (later improved in the events below).

checked_by.who: International Mathematics Research Notices (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2003 (per reference list in Lamzouri arXiv:2605.21476)

events.direction: Lower side (Ω). Consistent with the conjectured exponent; leaves the upper bound open.

events.what_happened: M. N. Huxley, 'Exponential sums and lattice points III', Proc. London Math. Soc. (published online October 2003, per the Cambridge listing seen in search). Gives Δ(x) = O(x^(131/416+ε)) for the k=2 divisor problem, the record cited in Wikipedia's Piltz section (citation [5]). The paper itself was not opened; the bound is taken from Wikipedia and from search summaries of the Cambridge listing.
events.delivers: Upper bound α₂ ≤ 131/416 ≈ 0.31490 for k=2. Restricted to k=2 (the main theorem is about lattice points in planar regions; the divisor exponent is a corollary).
events.remains: α₂ down to 1/4, and every k ≥ 3.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper online in October 2003

events.direction: Upper bound for k=2, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it. Superseded by the 2023 value below if that holds.

events.what_happened: G. Kolesnik (symposium paper, Durham 1979, published 1981, per the Wikipedia citation [8]); Ivić (1985, Theorem 13.2, citation [9]) also cited. Gives α₃ ≤ 43/96 for the k=3 Piltz problem. Primary text not opened; taken from Wikipedia's Piltz section.
events.delivers: Upper bound α₃ ≤ 43/96 ≈ 0.4479 for k=3 only.
events.remains: α₃ down to the conjectured 1/3, and every other k.
events.direction: Upper bound for k=3, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it.

events.what_happened: Upper bounds αₖ ≤ (3k−4)/(4k) for 4 ≤ k ≤ 8, attributed in Trudgian and Yang (arXiv:2306.05599, Section 2.4) to the citation key [HB81]. The page gives only the key; the paper behind it was not identified or opened.
events.delivers: Upper bounds for 4 ≤ k ≤ 8, e.g. α₄ ≤ 1/2 and α₈ ≤ 5/8. Restricted to those k.
events.remains: αₖ for 4 ≤ k ≤ 8 down to (k−1)/(2k), and every other k.
events.direction: Upper bounds, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it.

events.what_happened: Trudgian and Yang (arXiv:2306.05599, Section 2.4) attribute to [IO89] (Ivić and Ouellet) upper bounds for 10 ≤ k ≤ 20, and to Ivić's 2003 book (Chapter 13) the bound for k=9 and for 21 ≤ k ≤ 29. The primary papers were not opened; the list is taken from that section.
events.delivers: Upper bounds for 9 ≤ k ≤ 29 (older values). From the same section: α₉ ≤ 35/54, α₁₀ ≤ 27/40, α₁₁ ≤ 0.6957, up to α₂₀ ≤ 0.8009. The 2023 Trudgian–Yang values below are better for 9 ≤ k ≤ 21.
events.remains: Every αₖ for these k down to (k−1)/(2k).
events.direction: Upper bounds, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it.

events.what_happened: Siegfred Baluyot and Cruz Castillo, 'Sign changes of the error term in the Piltz divisor problem' (arXiv:2302.08003; v1 16 Feb 2023, v2 20 Sep 2023). For k ≥ 3, under the Lindelöf hypothesis there are at least X^(1/(k(k−1))−ε) disjoint subintervals of [X, 2X] of length X^(1−1/k−ε) on which |Δₖ(x)| ≫ x^(1/2−1/(2k)); under RH the intervals lengthen to ≫ X^(1−1/k)(log X)^(−k²−2). Methods: a second-moment bound for Δₖ(x+h)−Δₖ(x) by Selberg's method, and a fourth-moment bound for Δₖ(x). Abstract opened; the theorem statements were not.
events.revisions: v2 20 Sep 2023 deletes Theorem 1.3 (the unconditional k=3 case, which the authors say is superseded by earlier work), updates the introduction and adds Theorem 1.8. Journal version: Int. Math. Res. Not. 2024, DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnae189 (search summary).
events.delivers: Conditional results (Lindelöf or RH) about the size of Δₖ on many subintervals. No unconditional bound on αₖ and no change to it.
events.remains: Unconditional αₖ for every k.

checked_by.who: International Mathematics Research Notices (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2024 (acceptance date after the first arXiv posting)

events.direction: Conditional lower-side size statements, consistent with the conjecture. Not an exponent bound.

events.what_happened: Chiara Bellotti and Andrew Yang, 'On the generalised Dirichlet divisor problem' (arXiv:2303.05028; v1 9 Mar 2023, v2 6 Apr 2023). Abstract (opened): unconditional estimates on Δₖ(x) for large k, in particular Δₖ(x) ≪ x^(1−1.889k^(−2/3)) for all sufficiently large fixed k. A later journal version is reported in Bull. London Math. Soc. 56 (2024) (search summary, not opened). Trudgian and Yang (2024 version) attribute to [BY24] the bound αₖ ≤ 1−1.224(k−8.37)^(−2/3) for k ≥ 30 and quote 1−1.889k^(−2/3) for large k, so the constants differ between the sources I read.
events.revisions: v2 6 Apr 2023 (current version read). Bull. London Math. Soc. 2024 (search summary). Constant 1.224 with (k−8.37) appears in Trudgian–Yang's attribution to [BY24] but not in the arXiv abstract I read.
events.delivers: Upper bound αₖ ≤ 1−1.889k^(−2/3) for all sufficiently large fixed k. Restricted to large k below no explicit threshold given in the abstract.
events.remains: Every k below the threshold, and the conjectured (k−1)/(2k) for every k.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published journal version, 2024 (reported in a search summary; not opened)
checked_by.where: search summary only; no URL opened

events.doubts: The two sources I read give different constants for the large-k bound (1.889 in the arXiv abstract; 1.224 with (k−8.37) attributed to [BY24] in Trudgian–Yang). I did not resolve which is the published statement.
events.direction: Upper bound for large k, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it.

events.what_happened: Timothy Trudgian and Andrew Yang, 'Toward optimal exponent pairs' (arXiv:2306.05599; v1 9 Jun 2023, v2 6 May 2024, v3 15 Jul 2024). Section 2.4 'The generalised Dirichlet divisor problem', Theorem 2.9: 'By approaching the problem as a constrained optimisation, we obtain the following new estimates for αₖ (9 ≤ k ≤ 21).' The arXiv HTML rendering of v1 shows Theorem 2.9 already present, with α₉ ≤ 0.64697 up to α₂₁ ≤ 0.79803. The HTML renderings of v2 and v3 show α₉ ≤ 0.64720, α₁₀ ≤ 0.67173, α₁₁ ≤ 0.69156, α₁₂ ≤ 0.70818, α₁₃ ≤ 0.72350, α₁₄ ≤ 0.73696, α₁₅ ≤ 0.74886, α₁₆ ≤ 0.75952, α₁₇ ≤ 0.76920, α₁₈ ≤ 0.77792, α₁₉ ≤ 0.78581, α₂₀ ≤ 0.79297, α₂₁ ≤ 0.79951. These are fetch-tool readings of HTML, not checked against the PDFs.
events.revisions: v2 6 May 2024 and v3 15 Jul 2024 show different numbers in Theorem 2.9 from v1 (α₉ 0.64697 in v1 HTML, 0.64720 in v2/v3 HTML; α₂₁ 0.79803 vs 0.79951). The pages do not say what changed. No revision comment is listed on arXiv beyond '38 pages, 2 figures'.
events.delivers: Upper bounds αₖ for 9 ≤ k ≤ 21 (values above). Restricted to those k; nothing for k = 2–8 or k ≥ 22 in this theorem.
events.remains: Every αₖ for k ≤ 8 and k ≥ 22, and the conjectured (k−1)/(2k) for every k.
events.doubts: Theorem 2.9's numerical values changed between v1 and v2 with no explanation on the pages I read. This is a change to flag, not an error finding.
events.direction: Upper bounds for 9 ≤ k ≤ 21, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it. The result is by-product of an optimisation framework; the computation is numerical, not an AI system.

events.what_happened: Xiaochun Li and Xuerui Yang, 'An improvement on Gauss's circle problem and Dirichlet's divisor problem' (arXiv:2308.14859; v1 28 Aug 2023, v2 14 Sep 2023). Using the Bombieri–Iwaniec method, a new first-spacing estimate combined with Huxley's second-spacing results, gives Δ(x) = O(x^(θ*+ε)) with θ* = 0.314483… (Definition 1.1 gives 0.3144831759741…), improving Huxley's 131/416 ≈ 0.31490. Read from the arXiv HTML v2; the statement does not mention k and uses ordinary d(n).
events.revisions: v2 14 Sep 2023 (current version read). Journal publication not found.
events.delivers: Upper bound α₂ ≤ 0.3144831759741… for the k=2 problem only. Lowers 131/416 by about 0.0004. No k ≥ 3 content.
events.remains: α₂ between 0.31448… and the conjectured 1/4, and every k ≥ 3.
events.direction: Upper bound for k=2, consistent with the conjecture, not reaching it. The value 0.31448 is the k=2 record I found; Wikipedia's Piltz section (last edited 23 February 2026) still lists 131/416.

events.what_happened: Jean Bourgain and Nigel Watt, 'Mean square of zeta function, circle problem and divisor problem revisited' (arXiv:1709.04340; v1 13 Sep 2017). A search summary says Theorem 2 of this paper gives Δ(X) = O(X^(517/1648+ε)) for the k=2 divisor problem (517/1648 ≈ 0.31371), improving Huxley. The v1 text was not read. The page I opened shows only the abstract stub and a withdrawal note on v2.
events.revisions: v2 posted 16 Jul 2023 as a withdrawal by Nigel Watt (1 KB). Comment: 'A problem with the proofs of Propositions 2 and 3'; 'Theorems 1, 2 and 3 lose their status as theorems.'
events.delivers: Claimed upper bound α₂ ≤ 517/1648 ≈ 0.31371, which would beat both Huxley and Li–Yang. Withdrawn; does not stand as a result.
events.remains: If the withdrawal stands, α₂ is governed by the Li–Yang value and every k ≥ 3 is untouched.
events.doubts: The authors' own withdrawal comment: the proofs of Propositions 2 and 3 have a problem, and the theorems lose their status. I did not check which theorem holds the 517/1648 statement in the text of v1.

withdrawn.what: arXiv v2 (16 Jul 2023), withdrawn by Nigel Watt. Comment: 'A problem with the proofs of Propositions 2 and 3'; 'Theorems 1, 2 and 3 lose their status as theorems.' The 517/1648 statement is in Theorem 2 of v1 according to a search summary, not verified.

events.direction: Would have moved the k=2 upper bound. Withdrawn, so it does not move the record.

events.what_happened: Lahoucine Elaissaoui, 'On the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function and Piltz divisor problem' (arXiv:2406.00331; v1 1 Jun 2024, v2 15 Apr 2025). Abstract (opened): Fourier expansion of ζᵏ(s) for Re s > 1/2; claims a necessary and sufficient condition for the Lindelöf hypothesis; for almost all x ≥ 1 and every k, a series representation of Δₖ(x) as a limit with Laguerre polynomials in log x; and a Hilbert-space identity for ‖Δₖ‖.
events.delivers: Claims a representation of Δₖ and a criterion for Lindelöf. States no bound on αₖ. The Lindelöf criterion concerns ζ, not the exponent for each k.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: The claimed Lindelöf criterion and representation are unverified: no journal publication, no citing work and no review found in my searches. I did not read the proofs.
events.direction: Claims a criterion for the Lindelöf hypothesis, which is itself linked to αₖ ≤ 1/2 for all k (per search summary). It changes no exponent directly.

events.what_happened: T. Makoto Minamide, Yoshio Tanigawa and Nigel Watt, 'On the sum of Δₖ(n) in the Piltz divisor problem for k=3 and k=4' (arXiv:2412.11069; v1 15 Dec 2024). Abstract (opened): analytic properties of the Dirichlet series Σ Δₖ(n) n^(−s); Perron's formula is used to estimate the sums Σ_{n≤x} Δ₃(n) and Σ_{n≤x} Δ₄(n). Journal: Acta Arithmetica 216 (2024), 291–327, DOI 10.4064/aa230223-28-3; a publisher listing (search summary) gives online date 2 December 2024, which is earlier than the arXiv date and was not reconciled. Both dates fall in the window.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version read. Publisher listing gives online date 2 Dec 2024 (search summary).
events.delivers: Bounds for sums over integers n of the error term, for k=3 and k=4 only. This is a different quantity (a sum of Δₖ at integers n), not the pointwise exponent for Δₖ(x), so it bounds no Δₖ(x) directly.
events.remains: The pointwise αₖ for every k, including k=3 and 4.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper, vol. 216 (2024), per the journal reference on the arXiv page

events.direction: Concerns sums of Δₖ(n) for k = 3, 4. Does not cut either way on the pointwise exponent αₖ.

events.what_happened: Athanasios Sourmelidis, 'An additive application of the resonance method' (arXiv:2411.14221; v1 21 Nov 2024, v2 29 Apr 2026). Abstract (opened): improves Soundararajan's Ω-result for general trigonometric polynomials with positive Fourier coefficients, with consequences for lattice point problems including Dirichlet's divisor problem; the theorem statement was not read. Lamzouri's introduction (arXiv:2605.21476, opened) attributes to Sourmelidis and Mahatab together the improvement of the log₃ power for k=2 from −5/8 to −3/8, still without sign determination.
events.revisions: v2 29 Apr 2026: corrects minor errors, adds a proof of Chen's theorem and an acknowledgements paragraph (per arXiv comment).
events.delivers: Ω-lower bound for the k=2 divisor error term with an improved log₃ power (per Lamzouri's attribution; not verified in Sourmelidis's own text). No change to the x-exponent; no upper bound; no k ≥ 3 content seen in the abstract.
events.remains: α₂ upper bound; sign of large values; general k.
events.direction: Lower side at k=2: sharpens the log power of an Ω-result at the conjectured x-exponent 1/4. Does not move the upper bound.

events.what_happened: Runbo Li, 'On the Generalized Dirichlet Divisor Problem' (Preprints.org manuscript 202505.1432; posted 19 May 2025; v2 17 Sep 2025; v3 22 Sep 2025; DOI 10.20944/preprints202505.1432.v1). Per search summaries, claims better upper bounds for αₖ for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20 using newer growth-exponent estimates for ζ together with numerical estimates, described by the author as a minor improvement on Trudgian and Yang. Every Preprints.org page I tried returned HTTP 403, so the numbers were not read, and the description comes from search snippets only.
events.revisions: v2 posted 17 Sep 2025 and v3 22 Sep 2025 (search summaries; not opened).
events.delivers: Claimed upper bounds for αₖ, 9 ≤ k ≤ 20. Values not retrieved, so what the claim delivers is unverified.
events.remains: Every αₖ for k ≤ 8 and k ≥ 21, and the conjectured (k−1)/(2k) for every k.
events.doubts: Not peer reviewed (per a search summary). The numbers could not be read, so I cannot check the numerical method or the table of exponents. The author's affiliation in a search summary is a Beijing secondary school; that bears on qualification and is recorded for the later pass.
events.direction: Claimed upper-bound improvement for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20, consistent with the conjecture if the numbers hold.

events.what_happened: Kamalakshya Mahatab, 'Omega Results for The Divisor and Circle Problems Using The Resonance Method' (arXiv:2504.17032; v1 23 Apr 2025, v2 3 Sep 2025, the version read). Applies the resonance method to exponential sums with positive coefficients. Theorem 1 (divisor, k=2): Δ(x) = Ω((x log x)^(1/4) (log₂x)^((3/4)(2^(4/3)−1)) (log₃x)^(−3/8)). Theorem 3 (Piltz, general k, over the integers): for the maximum of |Δₖ(x^k)|/x^((k−1)/2) over X/2 < x ≤ 5X^(3/2)(log X)², the size is at least (log X)^((k−1)/(2k)) (log₂X)^(((k+1)/(2k))(k^(2k/(k+1))−1)) (log₃X)^(−1/2+(k−1)/(4k)). Both read from the HTML.
events.delivers: Ω-lower bounds for Δₖ over the integers at the x-exponent (k−1)/(2k), the conjectured exponent, with an improved log₃ power; for k=2 the log₃ power is −3/8 (from −5/8). Sign not determined. Gives αₖ ≥ (k−1)/(2k) on the Ω-scale; upper bounds untouched.
events.remains: Upper bounds for every αₖ; the sign of the large values; the integer-case log₃ removal for general k (Lamzouri removes it for k=2).
events.direction: Lower side (Ω) at the conjectured x-exponent; consistent with the conjecture; does not decide the upper bound.

events.what_happened: Nilmoni Karak and Kamalakshya Mahatab, 'The Piltz divisor Problem in Number Fields Using The Resonance Method' (arXiv:2506.22587; v1 27 Jun 2025, single version). Abstract (opened): improved Ω-bounds for the Piltz error term over number fields, obtained by generalising a Voronoi-type formula of Soundararajan to number fields and applying Mahatab's resonance result. Journal status is unresolved: one search summary gives Journal of Number Theory 281 (2026) 726–740, DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2025.10.013; a second search found no such record; ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403.
events.delivers: Ω-bounds for the Piltz error term over number fields (analogue scope, not Q). The abstract does not state the theorem; the 2026 follow-up by the same authors states the exponent η = (mk−1)/(2mk), which for degree m = 1 is (k−1)/(2k). Whether this 2025 theorem specialises to Q was not read.
events.remains: Integer-case Piltz upper bounds and sign for the integers.
events.direction: Number-field analogue. Lower side; does not directly bear on αₖ over the integers.

events.what_happened: Sebastian Tudzi, 'On the Generalised Divisor Problem' (arXiv:2506.21823; v1 26 Jun 2025, v2 20 Feb 2026). Abstract (opened): by the Dirichlet-convolution method, for k=3 the explicit bound |Δ₃(x)| < 2.968 x^(2/3) (log x)^(1/3) for all x ≥ 2, improving an explicit result of Bordellès; for k > 3 an explicit form Δₖ(x) = O(x^((k−1)/k) (log x)^((k−1)(k−2)/(2k))).
events.delivers: Explicit constant for k=3 and explicit log power for k > 3, both at the classical x-exponent (k−1)/k. Does not improve any αₖ, which is already known at smaller exponents (e.g. α₃ ≤ 43/96).
events.remains: αₖ for every k below (k−1)/k.
events.doubts: The constant in the v2 abstract is 2.968; an earlier search summary gives 3.369 for the same k=3 bound, which may be a version difference. Not resolved.
events.direction: Explicit upper bounds at the classical exponent. Consistent with the conjecture; no change to αₖ.

events.what_happened: Olivier Bordellès and Florian Daval, 'On a Smoothed Dirichlet Divisor Problem' (arXiv:2601.01905; v1 5 Jan 2026, v2 11 Jan 2026, v3 26 Jun 2026). Abstract (opened): asymptotic for the smoothed sum Σ_{n≤x} τ(n)(1−x/n) with main term x·P(log x) plus a constant (1/4 by the abstract), settling a conjecture of Berkane, Bordellès and Ramaré on the positivity of an integral of the Dirichlet error term. The abstract also records Hardy's result that the classical remainder is not o(x^(1/4)).
events.revisions: v2 11 Jan 2026; v3 26 Jun 2026 (current version read in abstract form).
events.delivers: A statement about a smoothed k=2 sum and the sign of an integral of Δ(x). Does not bound Δ(x) or its exponent. Neighbouring object.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.direction: Neighbouring result on a smoothed sum; does not cut either way on αₖ.

events.what_happened: Neea Palojärvi and Sebastian Tudzi, 'Explicit and Effective Estimates for the error term in the Generalised Divisor Problem' (arXiv:2603.16023; v1 17 Mar 2026, single version). Effective estimates for Δₖ(x) for all k ≥ 2 and completely explicit estimates for 3 ≤ k ≤ 9. Theorem 1.1 (HTML v1, read in part) gives |Δₖ(x)| < α_{k,j}(log x)^(β_{k,j}) x^(γ_{k,j}) in ranges x_{k,j} ≤ x < x_{k,j+1}. Examples: k=3, j=3 (x ≥ 1.601·10^98): γ = 859/1400; k=9, j=3 (x ≥ 1.601·10^72): γ = 1949/2200. Abstract: the explicit results 'improve the powers of x appearing in the known explicit bounds'.
events.delivers: Explicit bounds valid only for x above large thresholds (e.g. 10^98 for k=3). Their exponents are below (k−1)/k, but well above the asymptotic bounds already known for αₖ (e.g. α₃ ≤ 43/96; α₉ ≤ 0.6472), so no infimum αₖ moves. The improvement is over earlier explicit bounds, not over the asymptotic record.
events.remains: The infimum αₖ for every k.
events.direction: Explicit upper bounds valid for very large x. Consistent with the conjecture; no change to the infimum.

events.what_happened: Youness Lamzouri, 'Sharp omega results for the divisor and circle problems' (arXiv:2605.21476; single version, 20 May 2026, MPIM-Bonn-2026). Theorem 1.1 (HTML read): Δ(x) = Ω₊((x log x)^(1/4) (log₂x)^((3/4)(2^(4/3)−1))) and P(x) = Ω₋((x log x)^(1/4) (log₂x)^((3/4)(2^(1/3)−1))), with no log₃ factor. Uses a resonance method with a one-sided sectorial kernel (Gamma density) that works with the Voronoï phase. Improves Hafner's 1981 Ω₊ and Ω₋ results. Scope: k=2 (divisor) and the circle problem only; no general k (HTML read). No AI tool or LLM acknowledgement (HTML read).
events.delivers: Sharp lower bounds with sign for Δ(x) at the Hardy–Landau exponent 1/4 for k=2, with the log₃ factor removed. Sharpens the lower side at k=2; does not change the upper bound α₂ and says nothing for k ≥ 3.
events.remains: α₂ upper bound (0.31448 or lower), and every k ≥ 3.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of the Piltz number-field Ω preprint of September 2026 that builds on this method; Mahatab is author of the earlier resonance result that Lamzouri cites
checked_by.what_they_did: Use and extend Lamzouri's resonance argument (their Lemma 3.1 cites Lamzouri Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 2.1) and state that their theorem recovers Lamzouri's bound for K = Q, k = 2 (their Section 5.1). This is a use of the argument, not a verification of it.

events.direction: Lower side at k=2, sharpening the Hardy–Landau exponent; consistent with the conjecture; does not decide the infimum.

events.what_happened: Nilmoni Karak and Kamalakshya Mahatab, 'Omega bound for the Piltz divisor problem' (arXiv:2609.33820; v1 27 Sep 2026, single version). Abstract and HTML v1 (opened): for a number field K of degree m, Ω-bounds for the Piltz error term with η = (mk−1)/(2mk) on x log x, log power κ = α(Θ−1) (α = (mk+1)/(2mk)), with sign determined by kr₁ mod 8 (r₁ = number of real embeddings). Combines Lamzouri's resonance argument with a counting theorem for nonnegative multiplicative functions, removing the log₃ factor. The integer case with general k is not stated; K = Q with k = 2 appears as a special case (Section 5.1).
events.delivers: Ω-bounds with the conjectured x-exponent (mk−1)/(2mk) for number fields; for K = Q and k = 2 it recovers Lamzouri's bound. Analogue scope for general integer k.
events.remains: Integer-case Piltz upper bounds, and the integer-case log₃ removal for k ≥ 3 (not stated).
events.direction: Number-field analogue. Lower side; consistent with the conjectured exponent; does not bound the integer αₖ.

events.what_happened: Wenguang Zhai, 'A survey on moments of a class of error terms' (arXiv:2607.17249; v1 19 Jul 2026; Advances in Mathematics (China) 55 (2026) 481–504, per the arXiv record). disputes.summary: A search summary of arXiv:2412.11069 says Minamide, Tanigawa and Watt point out a gap in earlier work: Ivić asserted a bound for the integral of the truncated Voronoi formula for Δ₃, citing Titchmarsh, and Heath-Brown is reported to have noted that Titchmarsh omitted a condition required in Atkinson's original paper, which Ivić's use also overlooked. This is from a search summary; I did not read the full text of arXiv:2412.11069 to confirm it.

summary: Piltz divisor problem for all k: Δₖ(x) = Dₖ(x) − x Pₖ(log x), with the infimum αₖ of admissible exponents unknown for every k; conjectured value (k−1)/(2k). The lower side is established at the conjectured x-exponent. Hardy (1916) gives α₂ ≥ 1/4; Ω-results (Soundararajan 2003, Mahatab 2025, Lamzouri 2026 for k=2) show Δₖ is large at x^((k−1)/(2k)) up to log factors, and the in-window work is about the log powers of these lower bounds, which move but do not change the exponent. The upper side: α₂ ≤ 0.3144831759741 (Li and Yang, arXiv:2308.14859, 2023; a version of Huxley's 131/416 bound, which Wikipedia's Piltz section, last edited 23 February 2026, still lists as the record); α₃ ≤ 43/96 (Kolesnik 1981); αₖ ≤ (3k−4)/(4k) for 4 ≤ k ≤ 8 (Heath-Brown, cited as [HB81]); Trudgian and Yang (arXiv:2306.05599, June 2023) for 9 ≤ k ≤ 21, with v1 and v2/v3 numbers differing; and Bellotti and Yang (2023) for large k. All of these predate the window. In the window: Runbo Li's 2025 preprint claims further αₖ improvements for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20 (not read: Preprints.org returned 403, so the values and the numerical method are unverified and it is not peer reviewed); Elaissaoui (2024) claims a Lindelöf criterion and a representation of Δₖ (unverified, no review or citing work found); explicit constants by Tudzi (2025) and Palojärvi and Tudzi (2026), which hold at the classical exponent or only above very large thresholds and move no infimum; and Minamide, Tanigawa and Watt (2024), Bordellès and Daval (2026) and Zhai (2026), which concern sums of Δₖ(n), a smoothed k=2 sum, and joint sign changes of Δ₂ and Δ₃ respectively, and so are neighbouring rather than bearing on the exponent. Sourmelidis (2024, Mathematika) is credited with, together with Mahatab, the improvement of the k=2 log₃ power from −5/8 to −3/8 (per Lamzouri's introduction; not verified in Sourmelidis's own text). Lamzouri (May 2026) gives sharp Ω₊ and Ω₋ results for k=2 with the log₃ factor removed; Karak and Mahatab (June 2025 and September 2026) give number-field analogues, and the 2026 one recovers Lamzouri's bound for K = Q, k = 2 but does not state the integer general-k case. A close call: whether the log-power improvements to Ω-lower bounds count as 'bounding Δₖ(x)' depends on whether the bullet is read as upper bounds only; I have recorded them as events with their scope, not as moves in the infimum. Bourgain and Watt's 517/1648 (2017) was a claimed k=2 improvement, withdrawn by the author in July 2023 (the arXiv comment says Theorems 1–3 lose their status as theorems). Scope flag for the later pass: the frozen page's sub-bullet 'Dirichlet's divisor problem: the specific case of the Piltz divisor problem for k = 1' conflicts with the standard convention (Dirichlet is k=2; D₁(x) is trivial) and with the Piltz section of the same article, which uses α₂ for it; the dirichlets-divisor-problem record should be checked on that point. AI involvement: no event touching this problem names an AI system. Searches of the Anthropic zeta-zeros post (no divisor mention), the Wikipedia list of AI mathematical discoveries (no divisor entries), the AlphaEvolve and Erdős-problem literature (no Piltz or Dirichlet exponent result), and searches of AI-lab announcements returned nothing on αₖ. Two adjacent AI-involved papers are not this problem: Freiberg's arXiv:2609.15597 (14 Sep 2026), on the divisor function of n!, whose abstract says the improvement 'was formulated and proved during a private interaction with Claude Fable 5.1'; and the Umans–Wang refutation (arXiv:2608.06681, Aug 2026), which the search summary says came from an OpenAI Codex run and concerns arithmetic-progression divisor covers. The OpenAI openai/math release of October 2026 (722 manuscripts, 372 families) could not be checked directly: the repository was not opened, and the family summaries I saw include no divisor-function or Piltz family, so that absence is unverified. Authorship and qualification notes for the later pass: Lamzouri is at Université de Lorraine, CNRS, IECL (per a search summary) and his paper has no AI acknowledgement; Karak and Mahatab are at IIT Kharagpur (per a search summary; their acknowledgements list fellowship funding only); Sourmelidis's Mathematika acceptance is per the arXiv comment. Journal status is unresolved for Karak and Mahatab (2025; a search summary gives JNT 281 (2026), but a second search found no record and ScienceDirect returned 403) and for Mahatab's 2504.17032 (a search summary gives Ramanujan Journal 2026; unverified). Tudzi's constant differs between sources (2.968 in the v2 abstract; 3.369 in a search summary). Wikipedia's Piltz list of general-k bounds (for example α₁₀ ≤ 41/60, α₁₁ ≤ 7/10) differs from the Trudgian–Yang table (α₁₀ ≤ 27/40 older; 0.67173 new), so the frozen Wikipedia figures predate or disagree with that table.
competing_reading: A reader who takes 'bounding Δₖ(x)' to include lower bounds would count the in-window Ω log-power improvements (Sourmelidis 2024, Mahatab 2025, Lamzouri 2026, and the 2025 and 2026 number-field papers) as moving a named quantity, so that the in-window answer becomes yes on the lower side and no on the upper side. A reader who takes it as upper bounds only would count them as not moving the problem at all, because the x-exponent (k−1)/(2k) is unchanged. On either reading, the Runbo Li 2025 claim (αₖ for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20) would be the only in-window event that moves an upper exponent, if its numbers hold and the preprint is accepted; I could not read the numbers, so this rests on a search summary. Conversely, one could argue the Li and Yang 2023 value is not the current record if it is withdrawn or disputed, which I found no evidence of, or that Trudgian and Yang's v1 values, which differ from v2, were the ones in circulation at the window's start.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Runbo Li preprint text (Preprints.org, blocked from my fetches): its table of αₖ for 9 ≤ k ≤ 20 and its acknowledgements, to check the claim against Trudgian and Yang's v2/v3 values. (2) The Trudgian and Yang v1 PDF (unreadable from my tools) to confirm which Theorem 2.9 numbers first appeared in June 2023, and whether the v2 change is a correction. (3) The published versions and full theorem texts of Mahatab (2504.17032), Sourmelidis (2411.14221) and Lamzouri (2605.21476) to confirm the log₃ attributions, which I took from Lamzouri's introduction and Mahatab's HTML. (4) The publication status of Karak and Mahatab (arXiv:2506.22587) and Mahatab (arXiv:2504.17032). (5) The Li and Yang paper's journal status, and whether any published or refereed source has since confirmed or withdrawn it. (6) The statement's intended reading (upper exponent only, or both sides), which decides whether the Ω events count as bounding Δₖ(x). (7) A scan of openai/math CONTENTS.md for 'divisor', 'Piltz' or 'Δ', which would settle the AI search for the OpenAI release.

event.what_happened: Athanasios Sourmelidis, 'An additive application of the resonance method' (arXiv:2411.14221; v1 21 Nov 2024, v2 29 Apr 2026). Abstract (opened): improves Soundararajan's Ω-result for general trigonometric polynomials with positive Fourier coefficients, with consequences for lattice point problems including Dirichlet's divisor problem; the theorem statement was not read. Lamzouri's introduction (arXiv:2605.21476, opened) attributes to Sourmelidis and Mahatab together the improvement of the log₃ power for k=2 from −5/8 to −3/8, still without sign determination.
event.revisions: v2 29 Apr 2026: corrects minor errors, adds a proof of Chen's theorem and an acknowledgements paragraph (per arXiv comment).
event.delivers: Ω-lower bound for the k=2 divisor error term with an improved log₃ power (per Lamzouri's attribution; not verified in Sourmelidis's own text). No change to the x-exponent; no upper bound; no k ≥ 3 content seen in the abstract.
event.remains: α₂ upper bound; sign of large values; general k.
event.direction: Lower side at k=2: sharpens the log power of an Ω-result at the conjectured x-exponent 1/4. Does not move the upper bound.

events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author in July 2023: 'A problem with the proofs of Propositions 2 and 3'; Theorems 1-3 lose their status as theorems.
Claims a criterion for the Lindelöf hypothesis with no journal publication, citing work or review after more than two years; states no bound on any exponent.

Known only from search snippets (text returned 403), not peer reviewed, no uptake found, and the author appears to be outside the research community. It is a self-described minor numerical improvement on Trudgian–Yang rather than a landmark claim, so it is kept rather than set aside.

judgement.why: The statement asks only about bounding Δₖ(x) and names no exponent value, so the most anything could deliver is a bound on Δₖ for some k. I read 'bounding' as covering Ω-type lower bounds as well as upper bounds. On that reading the log-power sharpenings by Sourmelidis, Mahatab and Lamzouri move a quantity on the problem itself (the size of Δ over the integers) and count as bound. The number-field Ω papers change the setting, so they are variant. Tudzi and Palojärvi–Tudzi give explicit bounds at exponents worse than the known asymptotic record, which is an effective form of the problem rather than a move on αₖ, so they are variant. Sums of Δₖ(n), the smoothed sum and joint sign changes concern neighbouring objects and are also variant. Elaissaoui states no bound, so it is none. Runbo Li claims an upper-exponent improvement but is known only from snippets. Because it is a modest numerical claim and not a landmark one, the F10 threshold for not_credible is not met, so I kept it as doubtful. Bourgain–Watt is knocked down by its own withdrawal. Journal publication counts as digested; preprints count as unreviewed. No event credits an AI system.
judgement.doubts: Whether Ω log-power refinements count as 'bounding Δₖ' is a real reading question; if 'bounding' means upper bounds only, those events would be none, and the only in-window upper-exponent claim would be Runbo Li's unread preprint. The Runbo Li numbers were never retrieved. I accepted the pre-1990 classical results as digested on their standing in the literature, without primary texts.
